Order 
The present application under Section 528 of BNSS/482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed for quashing of First Information Report No.427/2023 registered at Police Station Mungaoli,
District Ashoknagar, along with all consequential judicial proceedings arising therefrom.

According to the case of the prosecution, the father of the prosecutrix appeared at Police Station Mungaoli and lodged a written report to the effect that on 27.11.2023 at about 5:00 a.m., when his wife went to see the prosecutrix on the bed, she was not found there.
On making inquiries in the nearby area, no trace of his daughter could be found.
He suspected that some unknown person had enticed and taken away his daughter.

On the basis of the information given by the prosecutrix's father, Crime No.427/2023 under Section 363 IPC was registered at Police Station Mungaoli and investigation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20847 2 MCRC-40454-2025 commenced.

During investigation, on 11.12.2023, the prosecutrix was recovered and her statement was recorded,
wherein she stated that on 27.11.2023, without informing anyone, she had left the house, took an auto-rickshaw to the railway station, and from there proceeded to Bageshwar Dham.
She stayed alone in the Ashram there for about 14-15 days.

She had left her home in anger as her family members were forcing her into marriage, therefore, she had gone away on her own free will without Govind Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3756666/

On this basis, the case was forwarded to the Superintendent of Police with a proposal for closure.

However, during the further course of investigation, the applicant/accused (Govind Tiwari) was arrested on 20.01.2025, and his memorandum was recorded, wherein he admitted to having enticed the prosecutrix, established physical relations with her, and having prepared forged birth certificates and other documents of the prosecutrix by fraudulent means.

Consequently, Sections 366-A,
376(2)(N), 376(3), 467, 468, 471 IPC and Sections 3/4, 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 were added in the case.

sentences.text:
Investigation by the police has been completed,
however, the charge-sheet has not yet been filed.

Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted before this Court that the applicant has not committed any offence whatsoever and has been falsely and maliciously implicated in the present case due to enmity.
The applicant has no direct or indirect connection with the alleged offence.

In the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20847 3 MCRC-40454-2025 present case, the applicant and the prosecutrix have solemnized marriage, and thereafter, they are residing together as husband and wife.

Subsequently, the parents of the prosecutrix took her away from the applicant's company, against which the applicant had preferred a Habeas Corpus vide Writ Petition No. 35453/2024 before this Court, which was decided on 20.11.2024.

In the said petition, as per the status report submitted by the State, it was recorded that the corpus had gone of her own free will,
whereas her parents had admitted that they were attempting to forcibly marry her against her wishes.

It is further submitted that thereafter, the applicant has also filed an application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act seeking restitution of conjugal rights, which is presently pending consideration.

Despite the fact that the investigation has not culminated into a charge-sheet in the present case till date, the police, with an intention to harass the applicant, had further registered another false case against him vide Crime No.282/2025 dated 26.08.2025 at Police Station Mungaoli, District Ashoknagar, under Sections 115(2), 126(2), 296, 351(3), 62 of BNS.

It is further submitted that the marksheet relied upon by the prosecution in support of the age of the prosecutrix pertains to a school which had already been closed about four years earlier, and hence, is unreliable.
The FIR against the applicant has been registered on false and concocted allegations, and he has been deliberately roped into the present case without any credible evidence.

It is further submitted that the medical evidence does not support the prosecution story and no injuries, either external or internal, were found on NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20847 4 MCRC-40454-2025 the body of the prosecutrix, and no definite opinion regarding commission of rape has been given.
The applicant never forced or enticed the prosecutrix.
On the contrary, she voluntarily accompanied the applicant to different places, and at no point of time did she raise any objection, complaint, or hue and cry.
It is further submitted the FIR has been lodged with an inordinate delay, for which no satisfactory explanation has been offered.
The applicant has not committed any wrongful act with the prosecutrix, and the allegations do not stand proved.
In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, no prima facie offence is made out against the applicant.

Hence, the FIR and all consequential Govind Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3756666/
2 proceedings deserve to be quashed in the interest of justice.

sentences.text: In view of the above submissions, it is prayed that this Court may kindly be pleased to allow the present application and quash the FIR registered vide Crime No. 427/2023 at Police Station Mungaoli, District Ashoknagar, along with all consequential proceedings arising therefrom, in the interest of justice.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection looking to the gravity of offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties, and perused the record.
The scope of inherent powers under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (pari materia with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973) is well settled.
Such powers are to be exercised sparingly, with great caution, and only to prevent abuse of the process of law or to secure the ends of justice.

The Court is not expected to conduct a mini- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20847 5 MCRC-40454-2025 trial or appreciate the sufficiency of evidence at the stage of investigation or prior to the filing of the charge-sheet.
The Apex Court in the matter of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, has clearly enumerated the categories of cases where FIR/ criminal proceedings may be quashed.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 6 SCC 116, it has been held that while exercising powers under Section 482 CrPC (now Section 528 BNSS), the High Court should not stifle legitimate investigation or interfere at an embryonic stage unless the allegations in the FIR, even if taken at their face value, do not disclose the commission of any offence.

entities.text: Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 6 SCC 116
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the FIR in question contains specific allegations against the applicant regarding enticement of the prosecutrix, sexual exploitation, and preparation of forged documents, attracting Sections 363, 366-A, 376(2)(N), 376(3), 467, 468, 471 IPC and provisions of the POCSO Act.
Whether such allegations are true or false is a matter of evidence which can only be examined during the course of trial.
At this stage, the Court cannot enter into disputed questions of fact or record findings on the veracity of statements.

The contention of the applicant that he has married the prosecutrix, or that she accompanied him of her own volition, or that medical evidence does not support the case, are all matters of defence which cannot be considered while exercising inherent jurisdiction.
It is also settled law that consent of a minor is legally invalid [Pls. see: Independent Thought v. Union of India, (2017) 10 SCC 800).

entities.text: Independent Thought v. Union of India, (2017) 10 SCC 800
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, such pleas cannot be grounds for quashing the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20847 6 MCRC-40454-2025 FIR.
In light of the aforesaid legal position and the facts of the present case, this Court is of the considered view that no case is made out for exercise of inherent powers under Section 528 BNSS.
The FIR cannot be quashed at this stage and the investigation is permitted to proceed in accordance with law.
